message.content: I'll take Connecticut. Cheap denial, and I still cover Pennsylvania Avenue.
message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to buy Connecticut Avenue or start an auction.

I have $573 and five properties. The opponent has cash and several railroads plus utilities. I am checking which color groups are already owned.

The opponent owns the light blue group, orange group, red group, and several utilities. I have no color groups yet.

Claude owns three railroads and several other properties. GPT has only Boardwalk. Most remaining spaces are unowned, including the pink group, Kentucky, Atlantic, and Pennsylvania Avenue.

I will buy Connecticut Avenue for $120. This leaves me with $453, enough to purchase Pennsylvania Avenue later. I do not need to sell my B&O Railroad. Ventnor blocks the opponent's yellow group. The light blue group is still incomplete.

Auctioning Connecticut Avenue would let the opponent complete a light blue monopoly and give GPT a foothold. The $120 purchase is only 21% of my cash. I am weighing whether the cheap house cost and high rent justify building a light blue group.

A complete light blue set requires buying Oriental from the bank and convincing the opponent to trade Vermont. That is difficult. Connecticut alone would only double rent to $16 before houses are built. The real question is whether $120 is better kept as cash. Claude's three railroads cost $100 each. The opponent's scattered properties currently pay low rent. GPT's Boardwalk pays $50.

I can mortgage my B&O Railroad for $100 if I need extra cash. I will not auction Connecticut Avenue because other players might outbid me.
